# =========================================================================
# JQI_PoliticalAttitudes.Rmd
#
# Political attitudes and employment quality
#
# Central question:
# Does measuring the quality of employment provide politically relevant
# information that is lost when employment is measured simply as
# employment status?
#
# Outcomes:
#   eqwlth   - support for reducing income inequality
#   getahead - beliefs about hard work versus luck
#   kidssol  - expectations about children's future standard of living
#   poleff11 - political efficacy
#
# Model progression:
#   1. Employment status
#   2. Employment status + social class
#   3. Employment status + JQI components
#   4. Employment status + social class + JQI components
#   5. Employment status + social class + prestige + JQI + income
# =========================================================================


# -------------------------------------------------------------------------
# 1. Packages
# -------------------------------------------------------------------------

library(tidyverse)
library(MASS)
library(broom)
library(haven)
library(here)
library(gssrdoc)


# -------------------------------------------------------------------------
# 2. Load data
# -------------------------------------------------------------------------

# If gss_job_quality_primary is already loaded, this section can be skipped.

gss_job_quality_primary <- readRDS(
  here(
    "01_tidydata",
    "GSS_Data_Cleaned",
    "gss_job_quality_primary_2000_2024.rds"
  )
)

# -------------------------------------------------------------------------
# 3. Construct political-attitude variables and controls
# -------------------------------------------------------------------------


jqi_political <- gss_job_quality_primary %>%
  mutate(

# =====================================================================
# EMPLOYMENT STATUS
# =====================================================================
wrkstat_num = suppressWarnings(
as.numeric(wrkstat)
),

wrkstat_factor = case_when(
wrkstat_num == 1 ~ "Working full time",
wrkstat_num == 2 ~ "Working part time",
wrkstat_num == 3 ~ "With a job, not at work",
wrkstat_num == 4 ~ "Unemployed / looking for work",
wrkstat_num == 5 ~ "Retired",
wrkstat_num == 6 ~ "In school",
wrkstat_num == 7 ~ "Keeping house",
wrkstat_num == 8 ~ "Other",
TRUE ~ NA_character_
),

wrkstat_factor = factor(
wrkstat_factor,
levels = c(
"Working full time",
"Working part time",
"With a job, not at work",
"Unemployed / looking for work",
"Retired",
"In school",
"Keeping house",
"Other"
)
),


    # =====================================================================
    # SOCIAL CLASS
    # =====================================================================
    # 1 = lower class
    # 2 = working class
    # 3 = middle class
    # 4 = upper class
    # 5 = no class
    #
    # Following the earlier class analysis, respondents identifying as
    # "no class" are excluded.

    social_class_num = suppressWarnings(
      as.numeric(class)
    ),

    social_class_factor = case_when(
      social_class_num == 1 ~ "Lower class",
      social_class_num == 2 ~ "Working class",
      social_class_num == 3 ~ "Middle class",
      social_class_num == 4 ~ "Upper class",
      TRUE ~ NA_character_
    ),

    social_class_factor = factor(
      social_class_factor,
      levels = c(
        "Lower class",
        "Working class",
        "Middle class",
        "Upper class"
      )
    ),


    # =====================================================================
    # OCCUPATIONAL PRESTIGE
    # =====================================================================

    prestige = suppressWarnings(
      as.numeric(prestg10)
    ),

    prestige = case_when(
      prestige >= 0 &
        prestige <= 100 ~ prestige,
      TRUE ~ NA_real_
    ),


    # =====================================================================
    # REAL HOUSEHOLD INCOME
    # =====================================================================

    realrinc_clean = case_when(
      is.na(realrinc) ~ NA_real_,
      realrinc < 0 ~ NA_real_,
      TRUE ~ as.numeric(realrinc)
    ),

    log_realrinc = log1p(realrinc_clean),


    # =====================================================================
    # EQWLTH
    # =====================================================================
    # 1 = government ought to reduce income differences
    # 7 = government should not concern itself
    #
    # Higher values = less support for redistribution.

    eqwlth_num = suppressWarnings(
      as.numeric(eqwlth)
    ),

    eqwlth = case_when(
      eqwlth_num %in% 1:7 ~ eqwlth_num,
      TRUE ~ NA_real_
    ),

    eqwlth = ordered(
      eqwlth,
      levels = 1:7
    ),


    # =====================================================================
    # GETAHEAD
    # =====================================================================
    # 1 = hard work most important
    # 2 = hard work and luck equally important
    # 3 = luck most important
    # 4 = other
    #
    # "Other" is excluded from the primary ordinal analysis because it
    # does not have an obvious ordinal position relative to 1-3.
    #
    # Higher values = greater emphasis on luck.

    getahead_num = suppressWarnings(
      as.numeric(getahead)
    ),

    getahead = case_when(
      getahead_num %in% 1:3 ~ getahead_num,
      TRUE ~ NA_real_
    ),

    getahead = ordered(
      getahead,
      levels = 1:3
    ),


    # =====================================================================
    # KIDSSOL
    # =====================================================================
    # 1 = much better
    # 2 = somewhat better
    # 3 = about the same
    # 4 = somewhat worse
    # 5 = much worse
    # 6 = no children
    #
    # Exclude "no children."
    #
    # Reverse the scale:
    # 5 = much better
    # 4 = somewhat better
    # 3 = about the same
    # 2 = somewhat worse
    # 1 = much worse
    #
    # Higher values = greater optimism about children's future.

    kidssol_num = suppressWarnings(
      as.numeric(kidssol)
    ),

    kidssol = case_when(
      kidssol_num == 1 ~ 5,
      kidssol_num == 2 ~ 4,
      kidssol_num == 3 ~ 3,
      kidssol_num == 4 ~ 2,
      kidssol_num == 5 ~ 1,
      TRUE ~ NA_real_
    ),

    kidssol = ordered(
      kidssol,
      levels = 1:5
    ),


    # =====================================================================
    # POLEFF11
    # =====================================================================
    # 1 = strongly agree people like me have no say
    # 5 = strongly disagree
    #
    # Higher values = greater political efficacy.

    poleff11_num = suppressWarnings(
      as.numeric(poleff11)
    ),

    poleff11 = case_when(
      poleff11_num %in% 1:5 ~ poleff11_num,
      TRUE ~ NA_real_
    ),

    poleff11 = ordered(
      poleff11,
      levels = 1:5
    )
  )


# -------------------------------------------------------------------------
# 4. Check outcome coverage
# -------------------------------------------------------------------------

jqi_political %>%
  count(wrkstat_factor, sort = TRUE)

jqi_political %>%
  group_by(wrkstat_factor) %>%
  summarise(
    n = n(),
    n_jqi = sum(
      !is.na(compensation) &
      !is.na(benefits) &
      !is.na(earnings_stability)
    ),
    pct_jqi = 100 * n_jqi / n,
    .groups = "drop"
  )


# -------------------------------------------------------------------------
# Examine industry assignments among non-employed respondents
# -------------------------------------------------------------------------

coverage_table_1 <- jqi_political %>%
  filter(
    wrkstat_factor %in% c(
      "Retired",
      "In school",
      "Keeping house",
      "Other"
    ),
    !is.na(compensation),
    !is.na(benefits),
    !is.na(earnings_stability)
  ) %>%
  count(wrkstat_factor, industry_common, sort = TRUE)

write_csv(
  coverage_table_1,
  here(
    "01_tidydata",
    "GSS_Data_Cleaned",
    "JQI_Coverage_by_EmpStatus.csv"
  )
)


# -------------------------------------------------------------------------
# Check how many respondents in each employment-status category have
# a valid GSS industry code
# -------------------------------------------------------------------------

jqi_political %>%
  group_by(wrkstat_factor) %>%
  summarise(
    n = n(),

    n_industry = sum(!is.na(industry_common)),
    pct_industry = 100 * n_industry / n,

    n_jqi = sum(
      !is.na(compensation) &
      !is.na(benefits) &
      !is.na(earnings_stability)
    ),

    pct_jqi = 100 * n_jqi / n,

    .groups = "drop"
  )


# -------------------------------------------------------------------------
# Compare industry assignment coverage by employment status
# -------------------------------------------------------------------------

jqi_political %>%
  filter(!is.na(industry_common)) %>%
  count(wrkstat_factor, industry_common) %>%
  group_by(wrkstat_factor) %>%
  mutate(
    pct_within_status = 100 * n / sum(n)
  ) %>%
  arrange(wrkstat_factor, desc(n))

political_coverage <- jqi_political %>%
  group_by(year) %>%
  summarise(
    n_eqwlth = sum(!is.na(eqwlth)),
    n_getahead = sum(!is.na(getahead)),
    n_kidssol = sum(!is.na(kidssol)),
    n_poleff11 = sum(!is.na(poleff11)),
    .groups = "drop"
  )

political_coverage


# -------------------------------------------------------------------------
# 5. Check outcome distributions
# -------------------------------------------------------------------------

table(jqi_political$eqwlth, useNA = "ifany")
table(jqi_political$getahead, useNA = "ifany")
table(jqi_political$kidssol, useNA = "ifany")
table(jqi_political$poleff11, useNA = "ifany")


# -------------------------------------------------------------------------
# 6. Helper function for ordered-logit models
# -------------------------------------------------------------------------

tidy_polr <- function(model, model_name, outcome_name) {

  out <- broom::tidy(model) %>%
    mutate(
      model = model_name,
      outcome = outcome_name
    )

  # broom::tidy.polr does not always return p-values.
  # Calculate them from the reported t/z statistic.

  out %>%
    mutate(
      p.value = 2 * pnorm(
        abs(statistic),
        lower.tail = FALSE
      )
    )
}


# -------------------------------------------------------------------------
# 7. Model formulas
# -------------------------------------------------------------------------

political_formulas <- list(

  # Model 1: employment status
  employment_status =
    ~ wrkstat_factor,

  # Model 2: employment status + self-identified class
  employment_class =
    ~ wrkstat_factor +
      social_class_factor,

  # Model 3: employment status + JQI
  employment_jqi =
    ~ wrkstat_factor +
      compensation +
      benefits +
      earnings_stability,

  # Model 4: employment status + class + JQI
  employment_class_jqi =
    ~ wrkstat_factor +
      social_class_factor +
      compensation +
      benefits +
      earnings_stability,

  # Model 5: full specification
  full =
    ~ wrkstat_factor +
      social_class_factor +
      prestige +
      compensation +
      benefits +
      earnings_stability +
      log_realrinc
)


political_model_labels <- c(
  employment_status = "Employment status",
  employment_class = "Employment status + social class",
  employment_jqi = "Employment status + JQI",
  employment_class_jqi = "Employment status + social class + JQI",
  full = "Full model"
)


# -------------------------------------------------------------------------
# 8. Function to run model progression for one outcome
# -------------------------------------------------------------------------

run_political_models <- function(data, outcome, outcome_label) {

  # -----------------------------------------------------------------------
  # Model 1: Employment status only
  # -----------------------------------------------------------------------

  f1 <- as.formula(
    paste(
      outcome,
      "~ wrkstat_factor"
    )
  )

  m1 <- MASS::polr(
    f1,
    data = data,
    Hess = TRUE,
    na.action = na.omit
  )


  # -----------------------------------------------------------------------
  # Model 2: Employment status + social class
  # -----------------------------------------------------------------------

  f2 <- as.formula(
    paste(
      outcome,
      "~ wrkstat_factor + social_class_factor"
    )
  )

  m2 <- MASS::polr(
    f2,
    data = data,
    Hess = TRUE,
    na.action = na.omit
  )


  # -----------------------------------------------------------------------
  # Model 3: Employment status + JQI components
  # -----------------------------------------------------------------------

  f3 <- as.formula(
    paste(
      outcome,
      "~ wrkstat_factor + compensation + benefits + earnings_stability"
    )
  )

  m3 <- MASS::polr(
    f3,
    data = data,
    Hess = TRUE,
    na.action = na.omit
  )


  # -----------------------------------------------------------------------
  # Model 4: Employment status + social class + JQI components
  # -----------------------------------------------------------------------

  f4 <- as.formula(
    paste(
      outcome,
      "~ wrkstat_factor + social_class_factor +
        compensation + benefits + earnings_stability"
    )
  )

  m4 <- MASS::polr(
    f4,
    data = data,
    Hess = TRUE,
    na.action = na.omit
  )


  # -----------------------------------------------------------------------
  # Model 5: Full model
  # Employment status + social class + prestige + JQI + income
  # -----------------------------------------------------------------------

  f5 <- as.formula(
    paste(
      outcome,
      "~ wrkstat_factor + social_class_factor +
        prestige + compensation + benefits +
        earnings_stability + log_realrinc"
    )
  )

  m5 <- MASS::polr(
    f5,
    data = data,
    Hess = TRUE,
    na.action = na.omit
  )


  # -----------------------------------------------------------------------
  # Extract coefficients
  # -----------------------------------------------------------------------

  extract_polr <- function(model, model_name) {

    coefs <- coef(summary(model))

    tibble(
      outcome = outcome_label,
      outcome_variable = outcome,
      model = model_name,
      term = rownames(coefs),
      estimate = coefs[, "Value"],
      std.error = coefs[, "Std. Error"],
      statistic = coefs[, "t value"],
      p.value = 2 * pnorm(
        abs(coefs[, "t value"]),
        lower.tail = FALSE
      )
    )
  }


  bind_rows(
    extract_polr(m1, "1. Employment status"),
    extract_polr(m2, "2. Employment status + social class"),
    extract_polr(m3, "3. Employment status + JQI"),
    extract_polr(m4, "4. Employment status + social class + JQI"),
    extract_polr(m5, "5. Full model")
  )
}


# -------------------------------------------------------------------------
# 9. Run pooled model progression for all four outcomes
# -------------------------------------------------------------------------

pooled_political_results <- bind_rows(

  run_political_models(

# ============================================================
# POOLED POLITICAL-ATTITUDE MODEL COMPARISONS
# ============================================================
#
# Model 1: Employment status
# Model 2: Employment status + social class
# Model 3: Employment status + JQI
# Model 4: Employment status + social class + JQI
# Model 5: Full model
#   + occupational prestige
#   + income
#
# Key comparisons:
#   M1 vs M3 = Does JQI add information beyond employment status?
#   M1 vs M2 = Does social class add information beyond employment status?
#   M2 vs M4 = Does JQI add information beyond employment status + class?
#   M4 vs M5 = What happens after adding prestige + income?
# ============================================================


# ------------------------------------------------------------
# 1. Function to fit the five pooled models
# ------------------------------------------------------------


# ============================================================
# POOLED POLITICAL-ATTITUDE MODEL COMPARISON
# ============================================================

run_pooled_model_comparison <- function(data, outcome) {

  # ----------------------------------------------------------
  # 1. Model formulas
  # ----------------------------------------------------------

  f1 <- as.formula(
    paste0(
      outcome,
      " ~ wrkstat_factor"
    )
  )

  f2 <- as.formula(
    paste0(
      outcome,
      " ~ wrkstat_factor + social_class_factor"
    )
  )

  f3 <- as.formula(
    paste0(
      outcome,
      " ~ wrkstat_factor +
         compensation +
         benefits +
         earnings_stability"
    )
  )

  f4 <- as.formula(
    paste0(
      outcome,
      " ~ wrkstat_factor +
         social_class_factor +
         compensation +
         benefits +
         earnings_stability"
    )
  )

  f5 <- as.formula(
    paste0(
      outcome,
      " ~ wrkstat_factor +
         social_class_factor +
         prestige +
         compensation +
         benefits +
         earnings_stability +
         log_realrinc"
    )
  )


  # ----------------------------------------------------------
  # 2. Create ONE common complete-case sample
  # ----------------------------------------------------------

  all_vars <- unique(
    c(
      all.vars(f1),
      all.vars(f2),
      all.vars(f3),
      all.vars(f4),
      all.vars(f5)
    )
  )

  model_data <- data %>%
    dplyr::select(dplyr::all_of(all_vars)) %>%
    tidyr::drop_na() %>%
    droplevels()


  # ----------------------------------------------------------
  # 3. Check outcome variation
  # ----------------------------------------------------------

  if (length(unique(model_data[[outcome]])) < 2) {

    stop(
      paste(
        "Outcome has insufficient variation:",
        outcome
      )
    )
  }


  # ----------------------------------------------------------
  # 4. Fit the five ordered-logit models
  # ----------------------------------------------------------

  m1 <- MASS::polr(
    f1,
    data = model_data,
    Hess = TRUE
  )

  m2 <- MASS::polr(
    f2,
    data = model_data,
    Hess = TRUE
  )

  m3 <- MASS::polr(
    f3,
    data = model_data,
    Hess = TRUE
  )

  m4 <- MASS::polr(
    f4,
    data = model_data,
    Hess = TRUE
  )

  m5 <- MASS::polr(
    f5,
    data = model_data,
    Hess = TRUE
  )


  # ----------------------------------------------------------
  # 5. Store models
  # ----------------------------------------------------------

  model_list <- list(
    m1,
    m2,
    m3,
    m4,
    m5
  )

  model_names <- c(
    "1. Employment status",
    "2. Employment status + social class",
    "3. Employment status + JQI",
    "4. Employment status + social class + JQI",
    "5. Full model"
  )


  # ----------------------------------------------------------
  # 6. Model fit statistics
  # ----------------------------------------------------------

  fit_results <- dplyr::bind_rows(
    tibble::tibble(
      outcome = outcome,
      model = model_names[1],
      n = nrow(model_data),
      logLik = as.numeric(logLik(m1)),
      AIC = AIC(m1),
      BIC = BIC(m1),
      df = as.integer(attr(logLik(m1), "df"))
    ),

    tibble::tibble(
      outcome = outcome,
      model = model_names[2],
      n = nrow(model_data),
      logLik = as.numeric(logLik(m2)),
      AIC = AIC(m2),
      BIC = BIC(m2),
      df = as.integer(attr(logLik(m2), "df"))
    ),

    tibble::tibble(
      outcome = outcome,
      model = model_names[3],
      n = nrow(model_data),
      logLik = as.numeric(logLik(m3)),
      AIC = AIC(m3),
      BIC = BIC(m3),
      df = as.integer(attr(logLik(m3), "df"))
    ),

    tibble::tibble(
      outcome = outcome,
      model = model_names[4],
      n = nrow(model_data),
      logLik = as.numeric(logLik(m4)),
      AIC = AIC(m4),
      BIC = BIC(m4),
      df = as.integer(attr(logLik(m4), "df"))
    ),

    tibble::tibble(
      outcome = outcome,
      model = model_names[5],
      n = nrow(model_data),
      logLik = as.numeric(logLik(m5)),
      AIC = AIC(m5),
      BIC = BIC(m5),
      df = as.integer(attr(logLik(m5), "df"))
    )
  )


  # ----------------------------------------------------------
  # 7. Function for likelihood-ratio comparisons
  # ----------------------------------------------------------

  lr_compare <- function(
    smaller,
    larger,
    comparison
  ) {

    ll_small <- logLik(smaller)
    ll_large <- logLik(larger)

    lr_stat <- 2 * (
      as.numeric(ll_large) -
      as.numeric(ll_small)
    )

    df_diff <-
      attr(ll_large, "df") -
      attr(ll_small, "df")

    p_value <- pchisq(
      lr_stat,
      df = df_diff,
      lower.tail = FALSE
    )

    tibble::tibble(
      outcome = outcome,
      comparison = comparison,
      lr_statistic = as.numeric(lr_stat),
      df = as.integer(df_diff),
      p_value = as.numeric(p_value)
    )
  }


  # ----------------------------------------------------------
  # 8. Likelihood-ratio tests
  # ----------------------------------------------------------

  lr_results <- dplyr::bind_rows(

    # Social class beyond employment status
    lr_compare(
      m1,
      m2,
      "M1 vs M2: Social class beyond employment status"
    ),

    # JQI beyond employment status
    lr_compare(
      m1,
      m3,
      "M1 vs M3: JQI beyond employment status"
    ),

    # JQI beyond employment status + social class
    lr_compare(
      m2,
      m4,
      "M2 vs M4: JQI beyond employment status + social class"
    ),

    # Prestige + income beyond Model 4
    lr_compare(
      m4,
      m5,
      "M4 vs M5: Prestige + income beyond employment status + class + JQI"
    )
  )


  # ----------------------------------------------------------
  # 9. Return results
  # ----------------------------------------------------------

  return(
    list(
      models = model_list,
      fit = fit_results,
      lr_tests = lr_results,
      data = model_data
    )
  )
}


# ============================================================
# 2. Run for all four political attitudes
# ============================================================

pooled_eqwlth <- run_pooled_model_comparison(
  jqi_political,
  "eqwlth"
)

pooled_getahead <- run_pooled_model_comparison(

  "getahead"
)

pooled_kidssol <- run_pooled_model_comparison(
  jqi_political,
  "kidssol"
)

pooled_poleff11 <- run_pooled_model_comparison(
  jqi_political,
  "poleff11"
)


# ============================================================
# 3. Combine likelihood-ratio tests
# ============================================================

pooled_lr_tests <- dplyr::bind_rows(
  pooled_eqwlth$lr_tests,
  pooled_getahead$lr_tests,
  pooled_kidssol$lr_tests,
  pooled_poleff11$lr_tests
)

print(pooled_lr_tests)

pooled_fit <- dplyr::bind_rows(

jqi_incremental_tests

jqi_over_employment_tests

# ============================================================
# COMPACT TABLE FOR PAPER
# ============================================================

# ============================================================
# JQI INCREMENTAL MODEL COMPARISON TABLE
# ============================================================

# ------------------------------------------------------------
# 1. Extract fit statistics for Models 1, 2, 3, and 4
# ------------------------------------------------------------

fit_wide <- pooled_fit %>%
  dplyr::mutate(
    model_number = dplyr::case_when(
      grepl("^1\\.", model) ~ 1,
      grepl("^2\\.", model) ~ 2,
      grepl("^3\\.", model) ~ 3,
      grepl("^4\\.", model) ~ 4,
      TRUE ~ NA_real_
    )
  ) %>%
  dplyr::filter(model_number %in% 1:4) %>%
  dplyr::select(
    outcome,
    model_number,
    AIC,
    BIC
  ) %>%
  tidyr::pivot_wider(
    names_from = model_number,
    values_from = c(AIC, BIC),
    names_glue = "{.value}_M{model_number}"
  )


# ------------------------------------------------------------
# 2. Extract the two key JQI LR comparisons
# ------------------------------------------------------------

lr_jqi <- pooled_lr_tests %>%
  dplyr::filter(
    grepl("M1 vs M3", comparison) |
      grepl("M2 vs M4", comparison)
  ) %>%
  dplyr::mutate(
    comparison_short = dplyr::case_when(
      grepl("M1 vs M3", comparison) ~
        "JQI beyond employment status",

      grepl("M2 vs M4", comparison) ~
        "JQI beyond employment status + class"
    )
  ) %>%
  dplyr::select(
    outcome,
    comparison_short,
    lr_statistic,
    df,
    p_value
  ) %>%
  tidyr::pivot_wider(
    names_from = comparison_short,
    values_from = c(
      lr_statistic,
      df,
      p_value
    ),
    names_glue = "{.value}_{comparison_short}"
  )


# ------------------------------------------------------------
# 3. Combine
# ------------------------------------------------------------

jqi_incremental_table <- fit_wide %>%
  dplyr::left_join(
    lr_jqi,
    by = "outcome"
  ) %>%
  dplyr::mutate(

    # Change in AIC/BIC from adding JQI
    delta_AIC_M1_M3 = AIC_M3 - AIC_M1,
    delta_BIC_M1_M3 = BIC_M3 - BIC_M1,

    delta_AIC_M2_M4 = AIC_M4 - AIC_M2,
    delta_BIC_M2_M4 = BIC_M4 - BIC_M2
  ) %>%
  dplyr::select(
    outcome,

    # JQI beyond employment status
    delta_AIC_M1_M3,
    delta_BIC_M1_M3,
    lr_statistic_JQI_beyond_employment_status =
      `lr_statistic_JQI beyond employment status`,
    p_value_JQI_beyond_employment_status =
      `p_value_JQI beyond employment status`,

    # JQI beyond employment + class
    delta_AIC_M2_M4,
    delta_BIC_M2_M4,
    lr_statistic_JQI_beyond_employment_class =
      `lr_statistic_JQI beyond employment status + class`,
    p_value_JQI_beyond_employment_class =
      `p_value_JQI beyond employment status + class`
  )


# ------------------------------------------------------------
# 4. Make the table easier to read
# ------------------------------------------------------------

jqi_incremental_table

# =========================================================================
# TEMPORAL ANALYSIS
# =========================================================================

run_year_models <- function(data, outcome, outcome_label) {

  # -----------------------------------------------------------------------
  # Years available for the outcome
  # -----------------------------------------------------------------------

  years_available <- data %>%
    filter(
      !is.na(.data[[outcome]]),
      !is.na(year)
    ) %>%
    pull(year) %>%
    unique() %>%
    sort()


  # -----------------------------------------------------------------------
  # Fit one model while allowing for model-specific missingness
  # -----------------------------------------------------------------------

  fit_polr_checked <- function(
    data_year,
    formula,
    model_name,
    outcome,
    outcome_label,
    year
  ) {

    vars_needed <- all.vars(formula)

    data_complete <- data_year %>%
      dplyr::select(dplyr::all_of(vars_needed)) %>%
      na.omit()

    # If no complete cases, skip this model-year
    if (nrow(data_complete) == 0) {

      message(
        "SKIPPED | ",
        outcome_label,
        " | Year: ", year,
        " | Model: ", model_name,
        " | No complete cases"
      )

      return(NULL)
    }

    # Check outcome variation
    outcome_values <- data_complete[[outcome]]

    if (length(unique(outcome_values)) < 2) {

      message(
        "SKIPPED | ",
        outcome_label,
        " | Year: ", year,
        " | Model: ", model_name,
        " | Outcome has fewer than two observed levels"
      )

      return(NULL)
    }

    # Check categorical predictor variation
    for (v in vars_needed) {

      if (is.factor(data_complete[[v]]) ||
          is.character(data_complete[[v]])) {

        n_levels <- length(unique(data_complete[[v]]))

        if (n_levels < 2) {

          message(
            "SKIPPED | ",
            outcome_label,
            " | Year: ", year,
            " | Model: ", model_name,
            " | ", v,
            " has fewer than two levels"
          )

          return(NULL)
        }
      }
    }

    # Fit model
    model <- MASS::polr(
      formula,
      data = data_complete,
      Hess = TRUE
    )

    # Extract coefficients
    coefs <- coef(summary(model))

    tibble(
      outcome = outcome_label,
      outcome_variable = outcome,
      year = year,
      model = model_name,
      n = nrow(data_complete),
      term = rownames(coefs),
      estimate = coefs[, "Value"],
      std.error = coefs[, "Std. Error"],
      statistic = coefs[, "t value"],
      p.value = 2 * pnorm(
        abs(coefs[, "t value"]),
        lower.tail = FALSE
      )
    )
  }


  # -----------------------------------------------------------------------
  # Run all models for one year
  # -----------------------------------------------------------------------

  run_one_year <- function(y) {

    data_year <- data %>%
      filter(
        year == y,
        !is.na(.data[[outcome]])
      )


    # ---------------------------------------------------------------------
    # Model 1
    # ---------------------------------------------------------------------

    f1 <- as.formula(
      paste(
        outcome,
        "~ wrkstat_factor"
      )
    )

    r1 <- fit_polr_checked(
      data_year,
      f1,
      "1. Employment status",
      outcome,
      outcome_label,
      y
    )


    # ---------------------------------------------------------------------
    # Model 2
    # ---------------------------------------------------------------------

    f2 <- as.formula(
      paste(
        outcome,
        "~ wrkstat_factor + social_class_factor"
      )
    )

    r2 <- fit_polr_checked(
      data_year,
      f2,
      "2. Employment status + social class",
      outcome,
      outcome_label,
      y
    )


    # ---------------------------------------------------------------------
    # Model 3
    # ---------------------------------------------------------------------

    f3 <- as.formula(
      paste(
        outcome,
        "~ wrkstat_factor +
          compensation +
          benefits +
          earnings_stability"
      )
    )

    r3 <- fit_polr_checked(
      data_year,
      f3,
      "3. Employment status + JQI",
      outcome,
      outcome_label,
      y
    )


    # ---------------------------------------------------------------------
    # Model 4
    # ---------------------------------------------------------------------

    f4 <- as.formula(
      paste(
        outcome,
        "~ wrkstat_factor +
          social_class_factor +
          compensation +
          benefits +
          earnings_stability"
      )
    )

    r4 <- fit_polr_checked(
      data_year,
      f4,
      "4. Employment status + social class + JQI",
      outcome,
      outcome_label,
      y
    )


    # ---------------------------------------------------------------------
    # Model 5
    # ---------------------------------------------------------------------

    f5 <- as.formula(
      paste(
        outcome,
        "~ wrkstat_factor +
          social_class_factor +
          prestige +
          compensation +
          benefits +
          earnings_stability +
          log_realrinc"
      )
    )

    r5 <- fit_polr_checked(
      data_year,
      f5,
      "5. Full model",
      outcome,
      outcome_label,
      y
    )


    bind_rows(r1, r2, r3, r4, r5)
  }


  # -----------------------------------------------------------------------
  # Run all available years
  # -----------------------------------------------------------------------

  bind_rows(
    lapply(
      years_available,
      run_one_year
    )
  )
}

# =========================================================================
# FORMAL TESTS OF TEMPORAL HETEROGENEITY
# =========================================================================

# -------------------------------------------------------------------------
# Helper for temporal likelihood-ratio tests
#
# Important:
# Restricted and unrestricted models are estimated on exactly the same
# complete-case sample. Unused factor levels are dropped before estimation.
# -------------------------------------------------------------------------

temporal_lr_test <- function(
    data,
    outcome,
    restricted_formula,
    unrestricted_formula,
    label
) {

  # -----------------------------------------------------------------------
  # Construct formulas
  # -----------------------------------------------------------------------

  f_restricted <- as.formula(
    paste(outcome, restricted_formula)
  )

  f_unrestricted <- as.formula(
    paste(outcome, unrestricted_formula)
  )


  # -----------------------------------------------------------------------
  # Identify all variables needed by either model
  # -----------------------------------------------------------------------

  vars_restricted <- all.vars(f_restricted)
  vars_unrestricted <- all.vars(f_unrestricted)

  vars_needed <- unique(
    c(
      vars_restricted,
      vars_unrestricted
    )
  )


  # -----------------------------------------------------------------------
  # Create one common complete-case sample
  # -----------------------------------------------------------------------

  model_data <- data %>%
    dplyr::filter(
      !is.na(.data[[outcome]])
    ) %>%
    dplyr::select(
      dplyr::all_of(vars_needed)
    ) %>%
    na.omit() %>%
    droplevels()


  # -----------------------------------------------------------------------
  # Make sure there are enough observations
  # -----------------------------------------------------------------------

  if (nrow(model_data) == 0) {
    stop(
      "No complete cases for temporal test: ",
      label
    )
  }


  # -----------------------------------------------------------------------
  # Check matrix rank
  # -----------------------------------------------------------------------

  X_restricted <- model.matrix(
    f_restricted,
    data = model_data
  )

  X_unrestricted <- model.matrix(
    f_unrestricted,
    data = model_data
  )

  rank_restricted <- qr(X_restricted)$rank
  rank_unrestricted <- qr(X_unrestricted)$rank

  ncol_restricted <- ncol(X_restricted)
  ncol_unrestricted <- ncol(X_unrestricted)


  # -----------------------------------------------------------------------
  # Stop if either design matrix is rank-deficient
  # -----------------------------------------------------------------------

  if (rank_restricted < ncol_restricted) {

    stop(
      "\nRank deficiency in restricted model.\n",
      "Outcome: ", outcome,
      "\nLabel: ", label,
      "\nRows: ", nrow(model_data),
      "\nColumns: ", ncol_restricted,
      "\nRank: ", rank_restricted
    )
  }

  if (rank_unrestricted < ncol_unrestricted) {

    stop(
      "\nRank deficiency in unrestricted model.\n",
      "Outcome: ", outcome,
      "\nLabel: ", label,
      "\nRows: ", nrow(model_data),
      "\nColumns: ", ncol_unrestricted,
      "\nRank: ", rank_unrestricted
    )
  }


  # -----------------------------------------------------------------------
  # Estimate models
  # -----------------------------------------------------------------------

  restricted <- MASS::polr(
    f_restricted,
    data = model_data,
    Hess = TRUE
  )

  unrestricted <- MASS::polr(
    f_unrestricted,
    data = model_data,
    Hess = TRUE
  )


  # -----------------------------------------------------------------------
  # Likelihood-ratio test
  # -----------------------------------------------------------------------

  test <- anova(
    restricted,
    unrestricted
  )


  # -----------------------------------------------------------------------
  # Return results
  # -----------------------------------------------------------------------

df_test <- attr(
  logLik(unrestricted),
  "df"
) - attr(
  logLik(restricted),
  "df"
)

tibble(
  outcome = label,
  n = nrow(model_data),
  lr_statistic = as.numeric(test$`LR stat.`[2]),
  df = as.integer(df_test),
  p_value = as.numeric(test$`Pr(Chi)`[2])
)
}

# -------------------------------------------------------------------------
# 17. Formal temporal test for the full model
#
# This asks whether the JQI relationships vary over time after accounting
# for employment status, social class, prestige, and income.
# -------------------------------------------------------------------------

# ============================================================
# Temporal heterogeneity tests: FULL MODEL
# Tests whether JQI component associations vary across years
# after controlling for employment status, social class,
# occupational prestige, and income.
# ============================================================

temporal_full_lr_test <- function(
  data,
  outcome,
  restricted_formula,
  unrestricted_formula,
  label
) {

  # ----------------------------------------------------------
  # 1. Construct formulas
  # ----------------------------------------------------------

  restricted <- as.formula(
    paste(outcome, restricted_formula)
  )

  unrestricted <- as.formula(
    paste(outcome, unrestricted_formula)
  )

  # ----------------------------------------------------------
  # 2. Identify all variables used in either model
  #    and create ONE common complete-case sample
  # ----------------------------------------------------------

  restricted_vars <- all.vars(restricted)
  unrestricted_vars <- all.vars(unrestricted)

  model_vars <- unique(
    c(restricted_vars, unrestricted_vars)
  )

  model_data <- data %>%
    dplyr::select(dplyr::all_of(model_vars)) %>%
    tidyr::drop_na()

  # ----------------------------------------------------------
  # 3. Drop unused factor levels
  # ----------------------------------------------------------

  model_data <- droplevels(model_data)

  # ----------------------------------------------------------
  # 4. Check that the outcome has sufficient variation
  # ----------------------------------------------------------

  if (length(unique(model_data[[outcome]])) < 2) {
    stop(
      paste(
        "Outcome has insufficient variation for:",
        label
      )
    )
  }

  # ----------------------------------------------------------
  # 5. Check model-matrix rank before fitting
  # ----------------------------------------------------------

  X_restricted <- model.matrix(
    restricted,
    data = model_data
  )

  X_unrestricted <- model.matrix(
    unrestricted,
    data = model_data
  )

  rank_restricted <- qr(X_restricted)$rank
  rank_unrestricted <- qr(X_unrestricted)$rank

  if (rank_restricted < ncol(X_restricted)) {
    stop(
      paste(
        "Restricted model is rank deficient for:",
        label
      )
    )
  }

  if (rank_unrestricted < ncol(X_unrestricted)) {
    stop(
      paste(
        "Unrestricted model is rank deficient for:",
        label
      )
    )
  }

  # ----------------------------------------------------------
  # 6. Fit models
  # ----------------------------------------------------------

  restricted_model <- MASS::polr(
    restricted,
    data = model_data,
    Hess = TRUE
  )

  unrestricted_model <- MASS::polr(
    unrestricted,
    data = model_data,
    Hess = TRUE
  )

  # ----------------------------------------------------------
  # 7. Likelihood-ratio test
  # ----------------------------------------------------------

  test <- anova(
    restricted_model,
    unrestricted_model
  )

  # ----------------------------------------------------------
  # 8. Calculate degrees of freedom explicitly
  # ----------------------------------------------------------

  df_test <-
    attr(logLik(unrestricted_model), "df") -
    attr(logLik(restricted_model), "df")

  # ----------------------------------------------------------
  # 9. Return results
  # ----------------------------------------------------------

  tibble::tibble(
    outcome = label,
    n = nrow(model_data),
    lr_statistic = as.numeric(test$`LR stat.`[2]),
    df = as.integer(df_test),
    p_value = as.numeric(test$`Pr(Chi)`[2])
  )
}

# Full-model temporal tests

     social_class_factor +
     prestige +
     compensation * factor(year) +
     benefits * factor(year) +
     earnings_stability * factor(year) +
     log_realrinc +
     factor(year)",

  "poleff11: Full model"
)


# ============================================================

temporal_full_tests <- dplyr::bind_rows(
  temporal_eqwlth_full,
  temporal_getahead_full,
  temporal_kidssol_full,
  temporal_poleff11_full
)

temporal_full_tests
